deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.
deletion_policy.rationale: Controls whether the Dataproc Autoscaling Policy resource can be destroyed. Requiring deletion protection prevents unintended destructive changes and makes the resource lifecycle itself a security-relevant control.

location.description:
The  location where the autoscaling policy should reside.
The default value is 'global'.
location.rationale: Determines the region/zone where the resource is created. Policy should restrict it to an approved-region whitelist for data residency; the allowed set is parameterised (a hardcoded example whitelist is acceptable).

policy_id.description:
The policy id. The id must contain only letters (a-z, A-Z), numbers (0-9), underscores (_),
and hyphens (-). Cannot begin or end with underscore or hyphen. Must consist of between
3 and 50 characters.
policy_id.rationale: Identifies the autoscaling policy by name; it is the resource label and does not itself control any security property of the resource.

project.description: The ID of the project in which the resource belongs. If it is not provided, the provider project is used.
project.rationale: Selects the GCP project the resource belongs to. Security is governed by that project's own IAM, org policies and controls, not by this placement field.

basic_algorithm.cooldown_period.description:
Duration between scaling events. A scaling period starts after the
update operation from the previous event has completed.

Bounds: [2m, 1d]. Default: 2m.
basic_algorithm.cooldown_period.rationale: Sets the wait time between scaling events. This is performance/stability tuning and has no bearing on the security posture of the cluster.

basic_algorithm.yarn_config.graceful_dec.description:
Timeout for YARN graceful decommissioning of Node Managers. Specifies the
duration to wait for jobs to complete before forcefully removing workers
(and potentially interrupting jobs). Only applicable to downscaling operations.

Bounds: [0s, 1d].
basic_algorithm.yarn_config.graceful_dec.rationale: Controls how long YARN waits for jobs to finish before removing workers. This affects job completion and availability, not security.

basic_algorithm.yarn_config.scale_down_f.description:
Fraction of average pending memory in the last cooldown period for which to
remove workers. A scale-down factor of 1 will result in scaling down so that there
is no available memory remaining after the update (more aggressive scaling).
A scale-down factor of 0 disables removing workers, which can be beneficial for
autoscaling a single job.

Bounds: [0.0, 1.0].
basic_algorithm.yarn_config.scale_down_f.rationale: Tunes how aggressively workers are removed. Purely an operational scaling parameter with no security effect.

basic_algorithm.yarn_config.scale_down_m.description:
Minimum scale-down threshold as a fraction of total cluster size before scaling occurs.
For example, in a 20-worker cluster, a threshold of 0.1 means the autoscaler must
recommend at least a 2 worker scale-down for the cluster to scale. A threshold of 0
means the autoscaler will scale down on any recommended change.

Bounds: [0.0, 1.0]. Default: 0.0.
basic_algorithm.yarn_config.scale_down_m.rationale: Sets the threshold before a scale-down occurs. This is scaling sensitivity tuning and is not security-relevant.

basic_algorithm.yarn_config.scale_up_fac.description:
Fraction of average pending memory in the last cooldown period for which to
add workers. A scale-up factor of 1.0 will result in scaling up so that there
is no pending memory remaining after the update (more aggressive scaling).
A scale-up factor closer to 0 will result in a smaller magnitude of scaling up
(less aggressive scaling).

Bounds: [0.0, 1.0].
basic_algorithm.yarn_config.scale_up_fac.rationale: Tunes how aggressively workers are added. Purely an operational scaling parameter with no security effect.

basic_algorithm.yarn_config.scale_up_min.description:
Minimum scale-up threshold as a fraction of total cluster size before scaling
occurs. For example, in a 20-worker cluster, a threshold of 0.1 means the autoscaler
must recommend at least a 2-worker scale-up for the cluster to scale. A threshold of
0 means the autoscaler will scale up on any recommended change.

Bounds: [0.0, 1.0]. Default: 0.0.
basic_algorithm.yarn_config.scale_up_min.rationale: Sets the threshold before a scale-up occurs. This is scaling sensitivity tuning and is not security-relevant.

secondary_worker_config.description: Describes how the autoscaler will operate for secondary workers.

secondary_worker_config.max_instances.description:
Maximum number of instances for this group. Note that by default, clusters will not use
secondary workers. Required for secondary workers if the minimum secondary instances is set.
Bounds: [minInstances, ). Defaults to 0.
secondary_worker_config.max_instances.rationale: Bounds the size of the secondary worker group. A capacity/cost parameter, not a security control.

secondary_worker_config.min_instances.description: Minimum number of instances for this group. Bounds: [0, maxInstances]. Defaults to 0.
secondary_worker_config.min_instances.rationale: Sets the floor for the secondary worker group. A capacity parameter with no security impact.

secondary_worker_config.weight.description:
Weight for the instance group, which is used to determine the fraction of total workers
in the cluster from this instance group. For example, if primary workers have weight 2,
and secondary workers have weight 1, the cluster will have approximately 2 primary workers
for each secondary worker.

The cluster may not reach the specified balance if constrained by min/max bounds or other
autoscaling settings. For example, if maxInstances for secondary workers is 0, then only
primary workers will be added. The cluster can also be out of balance when created.

If weight is not set on any instance group, the cluster will default to equal weight for
all groups: the cluster will attempt to maintain an equal number of workers in each group
within the configured size bounds for each group. If weight is set for one group only,
the cluster will default to zero weight on the unset group. For example if weight is set
only on primary workers, the cluster will use primary workers only and no secondary workers.
secondary_worker_config.weight.rationale: Determines the balance ratio between worker groups. An operational sizing parameter, not security-relevant.

worker_config.description: Describes how the autoscaler will operate for primary workers.

worker_config.max_instances.description: Maximum number of instances for this group.
worker_config.max_instances.rationale: Bounds the size of the primary worker group. A capacity/cost parameter, not a security control.

worker_config.min_instances.description: Minimum number of instances for this group. Bounds: [2, maxInstances]. Defaults to 2.
worker_config.min_instances.rationale: Sets the floor for the primary worker group. A capacity parameter with no security impact.

worker_config.weight.description:
